### 4176aeb3569bdca0b3d3f71c3f097322896a4922

[4176aeb3569bdca0b3d3f71c3f097322896a4922](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/4176aeb3569bdca0b3d3f71c3f097322896a4922)

Date: 2026-09-30T17:20:21-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: World & Visibility, Audio, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(dungeon-pressure): add phase change audio presenter and fix networked property weaving
```

#### Original body

```text
Implemented `DungeonPressureAudioPresenter` to handle global SFX on Dungeon Pressure Phase escalations using the local `AudioManager`. It uses `Render()` to ensure all clients play the SFX locally without RPC overhead.

Fixed a critical synchronization bug in `DungeonPressureController` by replacing `internal set` with public `set` in `[Networked]` properties. The previous access modifier caused Fusion's IL Weaver to silently ignore the properties, preventing the raid timer and state from updating.

Added explicit initialization validation for `DungeonPressureConfig` in `DungeonPressureController` to prevent silent null reference issues.

Added fallback warning logs in `EnemyReinforcementDirector` to detect cases where all reinforcement spawn points are rejected by the `MinDistanceToPlayer` constraint in small test maps.
```


```text
feat(dungeon-pressure): implement enemy reinforcement director
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduces ReinforcementPolicy on DungeonPressureConfig to dictate budget and spawn cadence per phase. Adds EnemyReinforcementDirector to periodically spawn reinforcements matching policy constraints and player safety distance. Refactors NetworkSpawnManager to expose TrySpawnReinforcement for safely injecting the correct origin.
```

### cb6990ed3498f85a8ff0329c2e86e0b6ac897a51

[cb6990ed3498f85a8ff0329c2e86e0b6ac897a51](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/cb6990ed3498f85a8ff0329c2e86e0b6ac897a51)

Date: 2026-09-29T18:26:49-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Inventory & Loot, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(commerce): polish Merchant UI layout and slot readability
```

#### Original body

```text
Polish the existing three-column Merchant layout without changing the
trade flow, rules or authority (COM-10).

- Inventory always renders SlotCapacity slots; empty slots show only
  their background with a disabled button, so they raise no selection
  or intention. Merchant stock is never padded. Slots are reused.
- Both grids use five fixed 96 px columns aligned from the top inside a
  vertical ScrollRect that only scrolls on overflow (30 slots = 5x6).
- Slot hierarchy: price top-left, draft badge top-right colored by side
  (+N purchase, -N sale), confirmed amount bottom-right.
- Center panel separates identity, scrollable properties/description
  and a fixed line editor: unit price, quantity, line total, line state
  ("Sin agregar", "Compra/Venta agregada: N"), Add/Update and Remove.
  Line total comes from MerchantShopInteraction.LineTotal via
  MerchantShopRowViewModel.TotalFor; the UI multiplies no prices.
- Footer has a summary row (Gold and slots current -> projected,
  purchase, sale, balance with sign, wording and color) above feedback
  with Clear and Confirm.

Tests: empty inert slots, slot reuse, sale line state, line total,
balance wording, five-column scroll grids, scrollable item text, footer
rows, slot anchors, LineTotal.

Docs: CommerceArchitecture.md prefab layout paragraph.
```

```text
feat(commerce): trade merchant drafts as one authoritative transaction
```

#### Original body

```text
Replace per-item merchant purchases with a pending trade draft of buy
and sell lines that is previewed locally and confirmed as one atomic,
authority-ticketed profile transaction (COM-01..COM-09).

- MerchantTradeDraft holds local lines, request id and in-flight state;
  MerchantTradePreview projects totals, balance, final-state capacity
  and typed blocks through ProfileInventoryRules shared with the store.
- TownMerchantNetworkController State Authority owns replicated stock,
  request dedup keyed by ProfileId + request id, reservations until the
  reported persistence outcome, and authority-priced tickets.
- IShopTransactionService / LocalProfileStore.TryCommitTrade apply one
  priced ticket atomically with receipt idempotency.
- TownMerchantTradeSession drives draft, preview, confirm, timeout and
  outcome reports; MerchantShopUI renders MerchantShopViewModel and
  raises intentions through MerchantShopInteraction only.
- LootDefinition gains BuyValuePerUnit; stocked definitions get prices.
- TownInventoryBinder composes the merchant presenter on SocialPlayer.
- Removes MerchantTransactionOrchestrator and ShopTransactionResponse.

Tests: draft, preview, ticket, feedback, interaction, session, UI
boundary/render, validator, wire codec, RPC, stock configuration,
profile inventory rules and trade persistence.

Docs: CommerceArchitecture.md added; LocalPlayerPersistenceArchitecture
updated for the trade transaction.
```

### 1c2616c4e6f84058cb964637bccf2a7f50b8c1e2

[1c2616c4e6f84058cb964637bccf2a7f50b8c1e2](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/1c2616c4e6f84058cb964637bccf2a7f50b8c1e2)

Date: 2026-09-29T01:44:30-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Movement, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(combat): aim accepted shield defense at the cursor like attacks
```

#### Original body

```text
While SecondaryAction is held and accepted as shield defense, the
character faces the cursor as it does for Attack and Interact, so the
player raises the shield toward the clicked direction.

- PlayerMovementNetworkController resolves the replicated
  FacingDirection toward the cursor when
  PlayerShieldDefenseNetworkController.CanDefend accepts the input
  buttons of the tick; SecondaryAction without a defendable shield
  keeps the locomotion facing. Invalid cursor directions use the
  existing movement and previous-facing fallbacks.
- The defensive cone and the six-direction shield presentation already
  read FacingDirection, so both follow the aim on every peer without
  new networked state.
- NetworkPlayer wires the movement controller to its shield defense.

Tests: PlayerMovementRules facing cases for accepted defense, secondary
action without defense and an unusable cursor; prefab wiring of the
movement controller.

Docs: PlayerMovementArchitecture and PlayerCombatArchitecture describe
accepted defense as a cursor-facing contextual action.
```

### b6a974ca79e288117ff599f8b64382660451a706

[b6a974ca79e288117ff599f8b64382660451a706](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/b6a974ca79e288117ff599f8b64382660451a706)

Date: 2026-09-29T01:44:20-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Movement, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): present directional shield defense on the Off Hand
```

#### Original body

```text
Present the replicated shield defense with six-direction Off Hand
clips, directional shield art and per-facing depth, and keep any Off
Hand visual on the drawn left hand through locomotion.

- Import the authored south Shield_Block source, retargeted to
  LeftHandPivot/LeftHand, and the six Shield-{N..SW} sprites with
  their original GUIDs.
- DirectionalAnimationGenerator bakes non-looping Shield_Defend_{dir}
  clips: the LeftHand trajectory turns with the facing under the Main
  Hand rule, rotation art and key times stay authored, OffHandGrip
  holds the facing's drawn LeftHand idle anchor, the hand keeps that
  idle sprite, and its sorting order is keyed per facing (-2 behind
  the body in N/NE, 32 over the main hand in SW, base 4 otherwise).
  Off-hand sources animating anything else are rejected.
- Idle and Walk body clips key OffHandGrip, stepped, on the drawn
  LeftHand centroid of every sprite frame, like WeaponPose, so Off Hand
  items follow the hand and enter Defend without a pop.
- Character.controller: IsDefending bool and a LeftHand-layer Defend
  blend tree on MoveX/MoveY with instant transitions from and back to
  locomotion. Base Layer and RightHand never observe it.
- PlayerAnimatorView only mirrors
  PlayerShieldDefenseNetworkController.IsDefending into the parameter,
  so every peer presents the replicated state.
- DirectionalShieldSpriteSet is presentation data referenced by the
  shield's LootDefinition, validated as Shield-only and complete, never
  by ShieldDefinition or LootId. PlayerWeaponPresenter shows the
  facing's sprite in every pose and, in front facings, draws the Off
  Hand item at least two slots over its hand.
- Fix the NW Walk hand sheets, whose left and right payloads were
  swapped, and rebase Walk_NW grips on the corrected centroids.

Tests: ShieldDefendPresentationTests (bake, source integrity, grip,
hand sprite and depth, renderer layout, stability),
ShieldDefendAnimatorTests (controller, runtime Animator per facing,
Main Hand isolation, sprite and sorting resolution, prefab wiring, loot
validation), and locomotion grip and NW identity cases in
DirectionalAnimationGeneratorTests.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture describes the Off Hand defense,
locomotion grip and sorting contracts.
```

### 097e9bd5d5d7d1d85031db25ddeb052cceec5669

[097e9bd5d5d7d1d85031db25ddeb052cceec5669](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/097e9bd5d5d7d1d85031db25ddeb052cceec5669)

Date: 2026-09-28T23:42:17-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(vfx): add provisional Great Hammer slash alignment to its strike
```

#### Original body

```text
Give Great Hammer its own attack VFX alignment, aligned to the real
strike of its six baked clips. No hammer impact art exists yet, so the
alignment provisionally reuses the shared Slash visual unchanged. It
must be replaced by a dedicated Smash/Impact visual when Art delivers
one. The change is data-only: no runtime code, no weapon branches, no
changes to the swing, the mirror contract or GreatHammer_Attack.anim.

Timing derived from the head (BladeTip) trajectory:
- The hammer winds up until 0.30 s, strikes from 0.40 s and its head
  reaches the facing (the impact) at 0.55 s in all six facings.
- StartSeconds 0.26: frame 0 anticipates the windup apex, frames 1-2
  cover the strike up to the impact and frame 3 the follow-through.
  Chosen from a sweep of start times as the one with the widest
  arc-containment margin that still covers the strike.

Geometry per facing (N, NE, NW, S, SE, SW), fitted to the head path
presented with the blade-axis mirror contract:
- Arc center and reach offset from the tip path grip + reach * axis,
  refined against the test's radial metric (<= 0.046 for the real
  reach and for 1.0 and 2.2).
- Rotation and mirror from aligning each Slash frame with the head;
  mirrored in every facing, sorting -9 north and 21 south.

Tests:
- GreatHammerVfxConfiguration_AlignsItsOwnProvisionalSlashWithItsStrike:
  its own alignment, distinct from the four swords'; pinned start and
  poses; measured impact at 0.55 s within Slash frames 1-2 in every
  facing.
- Great Hammer and two reach variants added to blade-tip tracing, the
  swing-sense check, the shared-visual check, the SecondaryGripPoint
  independence check and the presenter phase check (steps 6/10/14).
                                                                                                                                                                                                          cs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md describes the provisional alignment
and its timing.
```

### a45ea83978f3c76638cff987d5495488ef18aa9f

[a45ea83978f3c76638cff987d5495488ef18aa9f](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/a45ea83978f3c76638cff987d5495488ef18aa9f)

Date: 2026-09-28T22:56:05-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): add Great Hammer with across-facing two-handed poses
```

#### Original body

```text
Add Great Hammer as a two-handed catalog weapon baked from Juan's
GreatHammer_Attack.anim, and let held weapons whose authored pose lies
across the facing keep that pose in every direction. Long Sword and
Zweihander share the pattern and now keep their authored swing too.
Their source clips are unchanged.

Mirror contract: a left facing mirrors the held weapon across its own
art axis (sprite +Y) instead of the facing axis. PlayerWeaponPresenter
and DirectionalAnimationGenerator share
PlayerWeaponPresentationMath.ResolveAngleCorrection, which gives
-180 - AngleCorrection when mirrored. For -90 it returns the identical
value, so every other weapon is bit-identical; rebaking their clips
produced no content diff. No weapon branches, no new WeaponRig.

Great Hammer (great_hammer):
- 60 physical damage, 1.8 s interval, 1.5 range, 28 stamina, STR 15,
  PlayerMeleeAttackConfig, KnockbackForce 15 (linear extrapolation of
  low 5 / medium 10; Game Design only states "high").
- HandHeld + HoldsSecondaryGrip, AngleCorrection 180, grips (0, -0.375)
  and (0, -0.8125), rows 22 and 29 of GreatHammer.png, BladeTip (0, 1).
- Registered in LootDefinitionCatalog, DefaultLootContainerContentTable
  (weight 6) and RaidLootValueCatalog.
- GreatHammer set with six one-shot 1.05 s clips, not stretched to the
  1.8 s interval; no attack VFX.

Values derived from the sources' drawn hands, which move rigidly:
- Zweihander: AngleCorrection -90 -> 180; grips unchanged (5 px apart,
  source ~5.3 px).
- Long Sword: AngleCorrection -90 -> 180; grips (0, -0.46875) and
  (0, -0.71875), the first and last 3 px handle rows. The 4 px handle
  is shorter than the ~5.5 px its source animates.
- In all six facings both hands stay within 0.7 px of the handle and
  the strike brings the tip onto the facing, NW/SW included. South
  keeps every source curve except the re-derived second-hand X/Y
  (<= 1.2 px from the source path; Long Sword <= 3.5 px).
- Long Sword and Zweihander slash VFX poses (position, rotation, reach
  offset) refitted to the blade-tip path of their regenerated clips.
  StartSeconds, mirroring, sorting and the shared Slash visual are
  unchanged.

Tests:
- ResolveAngleCorrection values; the mirror is a reflection across the
  art axis for any correction.
- Weapons still at -90 keep a bit-identical held pose; existing
  two-handed clips bake identical to their committed assets.
- Great Hammer, Long Sword and Zweihander: hands on the handle and
  strike toward the facing in N/NE/NW/S/SE/SW; south keeps the source.
- Great Hammer catalog stats, set, geometry and sprite pixel
  derivation.
- Slash tip tracing uses the production mirror math; updated the pinned
  sword geometry and VFX poses.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md covers the mirror contract, the
weapons held across the facing, Great Hammer and the VFX refit.
```

#### Original subject

```text
refactor(animation): remove the unused LegacyRanged attack route
```

#### Original body

```text
No catalog weapon selects the LegacyRanged route any longer: every
weapon attacks through the generic Attack state driven by its
DirectionalAttackAnimationSet. Remove the dead route and the weapon
animation category that only existed to select it.

- Character.controller: drop the LegacyRanged-Attack state, its
  LegacyRanged-Attack-Directional BlendTree, its AnyState and exit
  transitions, and the WeaponAnimationCategory parameter. The
  RightHand layer keeps a single AnyState route to Attack
  (OnAttack && HasGenericAttack).
- Delete the WeaponAnimationCategory enum and remove
  _animationCategory, its accessor and its validation from
  WeaponDefinition.PresentationConfig and the 11 weapon definitions.
- PlayerAnimatorView drives attack presentation from HasGenericAttack
  and the attack-set overrides only; RefreshWeaponAnimationCategory
  becomes RefreshAttackAnimation.
- Keep the MagicWand_Attack_* clips: the Wand attack set still uses
  them.

Tests:
- The controller has no WeaponAnimationCategory parameter, only the
  Attack state, and a single AnyState transition to it.
- CatalogWeapons_UseOnlyTheGenericAttackRoute: every catalog weapon
  has a complete attack set and no weapon asset serializes
  _animationCategory.
- ConfirmedCatalogIdentity_UsesItsOwnGenericAnimation now covers all
  11 weapons, including Magic Staff, Long Bow and Compound Bow.
- The six-direction one-shot clip check reads the Wand attack set
  instead of the removed BlendTree.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md describes the generic Attack route
as the only attack route and drops the category references.
```

#### Original subject

```text
feat(vfx): add Bow Shot attack VFX with Compound Bow release alignment
```

#### Original body

```text
Compound Bow now plays the Bow Shot on its release. Its own
CompoundBowBowShotAttackVfx aligns the existing BowShotVfxVisual with
the Compound Bow attack, so both bows share one art asset and each
keeps its own alignment. PlayerAttackVfxPresenter and all runtime code
are unchanged.

- Starts at 0.4 s, the end of the Compound Bow stringing sequence, when
  the string hand leaves the hold; the 0.2 s shot ends inside every
  0.8 s attack clip.
- Each facing anchors WeaponPose at that release in its own baked clip,
  with the facing as rotation, so the shot follows the bow's shooting
  axis. No per-direction offsets are hand-authored.
- Reach offset 0.09375: from the (0, 0.09375) grip to the limb's front
  edge on the center column of RecurveBow.png. No blade tip is
  configured; the shot never uses the weapon reach.
- NW and SW mirror like the bow; sorting is 21 in front facings and -9
  in north facings, as for Long Bow.

Tests (Long Bow cases generalized over both bows):
- each bow references its own profile over the shared visual
- start matches the stringing release; blade reach never moves the shot
- origin on the bow front and axis along the shot in all six facings,
  with mirror and sorting
- confirmed attack plays the shot from release and clears it
- PlayerAttackVfxPresenter added to the weapon-identity runtime check
- RejectedAttack_ClearsPendingEffect uses the Shield, since every
  catalog weapon now has an Attack VFX

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture describes Compound Bow as the second
Bow Shot consumer.
```

[3580ff0dac0be47aaae2c86f424cc68640568b04](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/3580ff0dac0be47aaae2c86f424cc68640568b04)

Date: 2026-09-28T18:55:47-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): animate Compound Bow string draw during its attack
```

#### Original body

```text
Compound Bow now draws, holds and releases its string during the
confirmed attack through its own WeaponAttackSpriteAnimation. Only the
held weapon's sprite changes: WeaponPose, both hands, GripPoint,
AngleCorrection, facing, mirror, sorting and the directional bake are
unchanged, and no runtime code is added.

- Weapon-CompoundBow-Stringing.png is rotated 90 degrees
  counterclockwise into the world sprite's orientation (limb up, string
  on the bottom row), like the Long Bow sheet. Pixels are unchanged.
- Sprite rects are fitted to each frame, at 16 PPU with point filtering.
  Each pivot sits 3 px below the top of the limb on the center column,
  so the (0, 0.09375) grip stays on the limb's center in every frame.
- CompoundBowStringingAttackSpriteAnimation follows the Compound Bow's
  own baked attack rather than Long Bow's timing: rest from 0.1 s,
  partial draws at 0.2 s and 0.25 s, full draw at 0.3 s while the hands
  peak at 0.35 s, hold, and the world sprite at 0.4 s when the string
  hand leaves the hold.
- The rest frame spans the world sprite's 23 px and grip but is one row
  deeper than RecurveBow.png, so the string shifts by one pixel when
  the sequence starts and at the release.

Tests (Long Bow cases generalized over both bows):
- each bow references its own stringing; other weapons have none
- draw, hold and release timing derived from each bow's baked hold
- frames keep PPU, point filtering, grip and the world sprite's span
- presenter swaps only the sprite, only inside the confirmed attack
- Long Bow keeps its pixel-identical rest frame check

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture describes the Compound Bow stringing,
its geometry and timing.
```

[cdd176b58b82494a41ebaabd903dd617e35c66ae](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/cdd176b58b82494a41ebaabd903dd617e35c66ae)

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): migrate Compound Bow to a weapon-driven directional attack
```

#### Original body

```text
Compound Bow leaves the LegacyRanged fallback and plays the generic
Attack route through its own DirectionalAttackAnimationSet, baked by
the existing weapon-driven rig: WeaponPose owns the bow, the left hand
holds its grip and the right hand draws the string. The WeaponDriven
contract is reused unchanged; the bow only adds its own geometry and
clips.

- DirectionalAnimationGenerator.GenerateAssets takes an optional source
  name, so Compound Bow bakes from RecurveBow_Attack.anim (left
  untouched) into CompoundBow_Attack_<Facing> clips. New menu item:
  Tools/Animations/Generate Compound Bow Directional Attacks.
- CompoundBowWeaponDefinition: category None, CompoundBow set,
  Rig WeaponDriven, SecondHand FollowsAuthoredMotion, AngleCorrection
  -90 and GripPoint (0, 0.09375), the center of the three-row limb on
  the center column of the 23x6 px RecurveBow.png.
- The clip keeps its authored timing: 0.6 s plus the 0.1 s blends on
  each side (0.8 s). It is not stretched to the 1.8 s attack interval.
- Recurve draws to chest height, so its lower aim center brings the
  north-facing bow closer to the body than Long Bow's.
- No catalog weapon uses LegacyRanged any longer; the route is kept
  and its removal is a separate follow-up.

Tests (Long Bow cases generalized over both bows):
- complete six-clip set and stable regeneration
- two-handed generic Attack with WeaponDriven rig
- grip derived from the sprite, shot along the facing in all facings
- WeaponPose/hand invariants, south reconstructs the source
- bow projected toward the target; draw and release read from the
  authored hold
- catalog and animator expectations moved from LegacyRanged to None

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture describes Compound Bow on the
weapon-driven rig, its geometry, timing and the unused LegacyRanged
route.
```

### 8b9ffbb689b4bc94601ada12fef77263c71248a5

[8b9ffbb689b4bc94601ada12fef77263c71248a5](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/8b9ffbb689b4bc94601ada12fef77263c71248a5)

Date: 2026-09-28T18:00:49-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(vfx): add Bow Shot attack VFX with Long Bow release alignment
```

#### Original body

```text
Long Bow now plays a Bow Shot impulse on its confirmed attack. The shot
starts at the string release that the stringing sequence already
defines, and leaves the bow's front along its shooting axis in all six
facings. It does not use a fabricated blade tip.

Generalize attack VFX sizing so it no longer always needs a blade:
- AttackVfxVisualDefinition declares UsesWeaponReach, which defaults to
  true. Such visuals keep resolving from ReachOffset + BladeReach, so
  Slash, Thrust and Cast Flash resolve exactly as before.
- A visual that does not use the weapon reach resolves from its pose's
  ReachOffset alone. WeaponDefinition requires a blade tip distinct
  from the grip point only for visuals that use the weapon reach.
- PlayerAttackVfxPresenter is unchanged. It has no branch per visual
  type or per weapon.

Add BowShotVfxVisualDefinition, reusable release impulse art:
- UsesWeaponReach is false. Its Origin, in sprite local units, sits on
  the shot origin in every frame.
- The art points along the pose axis at native pixel scale and mirrors
  across it like the bow. It is an impulse, not a trajectory, so
  neither the blade reach nor the projectile's range sizes it.

Fix the VFX-BowShot.png import to match the art:
- The sheet is four 96x96 px cells, the same layout as the other VFX
  sheets: release flash, streak, rings and remnants, traveling along
  +X on one axis. The old slicing (8x9 and 223x19) cut frame 0 and
  merged the other three frames into one sprite.
- Four centered cells at 16 PPU, point filtering, no compression.
- The flash center, (-0.875, -0.03125), is the shared origin.
- BowShotVfx.anim plays the four frames at 50 ms each on
  AttackVfx/SpriteRenderer.m_Sprite, once, over 0.2 s.

LongBowBowShotAttackVfx aligns the visual with the Long Bow:
- It starts at 0.45 s, the EndSeconds of the stringing sequence, when
  the string hand releases. The stringing stays the single source of
  that timing. The shot ends at 0.65 s, inside every 0.9 s clip.
- Each facing anchors the bow's pivot at the release, sampled from the
  baked clips: the grip on WeaponPose, rotated to the facing's shooting
  axis.
- ReachOffset is 0.09375, the distance from the grip to the limb's
  front edge in LongBow.png, the same in every facing.
- NW and SW are mirrored like the bow. Sorting is 21 in front facings
  and -9 in north facings.
- No per-direction offsets and no blade tip are configured.

Tests:
- BowShotPresentationTests: import and cell layout; origin derived from
  the flash; the clip; only Bow Shot ignores the weapon reach;
  reach-based VFX resolve as before; Long Bow validates without a
  blade and blade reach never moves or resizes the shot; start tied to
  the stringing release; poses re-derived from the prefab in six
  facings; the real presenter LateUpdate shows nothing before 0.45 s,
  frames 0-3 until 0.65 s, then clears; the confirmed effect survives
  an equipment lookup failure mid-attack.
- DirectionalAttackAnimationSetTests now expects the Long Bow Bow Shot
  VFX. RejectedAttack_ClearsPendingEffect uses Compound Bow as the
  weapon without a VFX.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md documents UsesWeaponReach, the Bow
Shot visual and the Long Bow alignment.
```

### 2f001775eb316e1161e73bc151f64a5a392489be

[2f001775eb316e1161e73bc151f64a5a392489be](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/2f001775eb316e1161e73bc151f64a5a392489be)

Date: 2026-09-28T17:41:23-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): animate Long Bow string draw during its attack
```

#### Original body

```text
Long Bow now draws, holds and releases its string during the confirmed
attack. The frames follow the same baked attack clip that drives
WeaponPose and both hands. Only the held weapon's sprite changes: its
pose, GripPoint, AngleCorrection, facing and mirror are unchanged.

Add WeaponAttackSpriteAnimation, an optional presentation asset
referenced from WeaponDefinition.Presentation.AttackSpriteAnimation:
- StartSeconds in attack clip time, plus ordered frames of a sprite
  and a positive duration.
- Validation requires a complete attack animation set and a sequence
  that ends inside all six attack clips.
- Before the start, after the last frame and outside the attack, the
  weapon shows its world sprite. Weapons without the asset behave as
  before.

Runtime stays generic and local:
- PlayerAnimatorView.TryGetPresentedAttackSeconds returns the clip time
  only while the RightHand layer plays an Attack state whose clip
  belongs to the pinned attack weapon's own set.
- PlayerWeaponPresenter resolves the frame through
  PlayerWeaponPresentationMath.ResolveMainHandSprite and swaps only the
  renderer sprite. It adds no Animator, layer, controller, networked
  state or weapon identity branch. The attack VFX pipeline is untouched.

Long Bow stringing sheet:
- The sheet was drawn rotated 90 degrees from the world sprite: frame 0
  rotated counter-clockwise is pixel-identical to LongBow.png. Rotate it
  in place so the frames share the world sprite's orientation,
  AngleCorrection (-90) and GripPoint (0, 0.125).
- Import settings: 16 PPU, point filtering, no compression, tight frame
  rects, and custom pivots on the center column 3.5 px below the top of
  the limb, so the grip lands on the same pixel in every frame.
- LongBowStringingAttackSpriteAnimation starts at 0.1 s, when the
  ease-in ends. Frames: rest 0.10-0.20, partial draws 0.20-0.25 and
  0.25-0.35, full draw and hold 0.35-0.45. The string releases at
  0.45 s, when the string hand leaves the hold. One sequence serves all
  six facings.

Tests (WeaponAttackSpriteAnimationTests):
- frame window boundaries and validation rules;
- every weapon except Long Bow has no attack sprite animation;
- Long Bow references its asset, timing and frames and keeps its
  weapon-driven pose values;
- every frame keeps 16 PPU, point filtering and the grip on the center
  of the limb, and frame 0 matches the world sprite pixel for pixel;
- presenter on NetworkPlayer.prefab with the real Animator: the sprite
  changes in sync with the attack clip time while the weapon visual's
  position, rotation and scale stay unchanged, and Idle falls outside
  the attack window;
- a clip outside the pinned weapon's set never plays its frames;
- presenter, math, animator view and asset code do not depend on the
  weapon's identity.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md documents the contract and the Long
Bow configuration.
```

### 59ff19a2698e2c773b2447479af84c432a817ac8

[59ff19a2698e2c773b2447479af84c432a817ac8](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/59ff19a2698e2c773b2447479af84c432a817ac8)

Date: 2026-09-28T17:09:01-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Movement, Inventory & Loot, UI, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): migrate Long Bow to a weapon-driven directional attack
```

#### Original body

```text
Bake the south-authored LongBow_Attack.anim into six one-shot
directional clips (N, NE, NW, S, SE, SW). Add a LongBow
DirectionalAttackAnimationSet and move the bow from LegacyRanged to the
generic Attack route (category None).

The authored clip shows a right-handed archer. The left hand is the bow
arm and pushes toward the target. The right hand draws the string toward
the face and releases it. A rigid bow sprite cannot follow a hand-held
rig, so add WeaponRig to WeaponDefinition.Presentation:
- HandHeld (default): the single weapon visual follows MainHandGrip.
  Every other weapon is unchanged.
- WeaponDriven: the weapon owns its pose. PlayerWeaponPresenter
  reparents the same visual to WeaponPose, a new transform under
  VisualRoot that sits inside no hand. Validation allows it only for
  two-handed weapons whose second hand is FollowsAuthoredMotion.

Weapon-driven bake contract:
- The south source is read as drawn positions: each hand transform
  plus its idle sprite anchor.
- The left hand becomes the WeaponPose trajectory and the right hand
  becomes the string target. Both turn with the facing about the aim
  center: the body axis at the string-hand height of the authored
  draw hold. This keeps the aim height, so N draws upward instead of
  toward the feet.
- Both runtime hands are keyed so their drawn centroids land on those
  points. The bow hand always holds the grip, and the string hand
  never moves the bow. South reproduces the source exactly.
- The clip eases in from, and back out to, the facing's locomotion pose
  over 0.1 s on each side, because the source starts in a ready pose and
  the Attack transitions are instant. The clip is 0.9 s long, matching
  the bow's attack interval.
- In S, SE and SW the bow hand sorts at 25: over the bow (20) and its
  VFX (21), under the main hand (30).

Outside attacks, WeaponPose rests in the drawn left hand. The new
"Generate Weapon Pose Locomotion" menu keys it in every Idle and Walk
clip at each LeftHand sprite frame.

Long Bow configuration, derived from the 27x7 px LongBow.png:
- GripPoint (0, 0.125): the center of the limb in the center column.
- AngleCorrection -90: the sprite shoots along +Y.

LegacyRanged remains only for Compound Bow.

Tests:
- Weapon-driven clip contract in six facings: grip invariant, aim-center
  turn, authored timing and rotation art, locomotion rest at both ends,
  forward-of-body invariant, and bow-hand sorting.
- WeaponPose locomotion keys in all Idle and Walk clips.
- HandHeld outputs do not animate WeaponPose.
- WeaponDriven validation.
- LongBow set, GripPoint derived from the sprite pixels, and presenter
  orientation in six facings.
- Prefab hierarchy with a single weapon visual and WeaponPose outside
  the hands.
- Catalog and Animator expectations for Long Bow on generic Attack.

Document the weapon rig in PlayerCombatArchitecture.md.
```

```text
feat(vfx): add Cast Flash attack VFX with Magic Staff alignment
```

#### Original body

```text
Make Magic Staff the second consumer of the shared CastFlashVfxVisual
through its own MagicStaffCastFlashAttackVfx alignment. The art, the
clip and the presenter are reused unchanged, and the Cast Flash
contract needed no changes.

Derived from MagicStaff.png and the six staff directional clips:
- BladeTip (-0.0625, 0.53125): the center of the 5x5 px gem of the
  13x24 px sprite. Reach from the grip is 1.0331.
- The cast is at 0.9s in every facing, when the forward strike peaks.
  startSeconds 0.875 ignites frame 0 as the gem arrives, and frames
  2-3 fade in place while the staff recovers.
- Each pose anchors the main-hand grip at the peak and uses the grip
  to gem axis as its rotation, with no reach offset. Sorting is 21 in
  front facings and -9 in north facings, just above the held staff.

The staff's left hand is an independent authored gesture outside the
main-hand chain, so it never moves the cast point.

Generalize the Cast Flash tests per caster (Wand and Staff) and add
tests for:
- the staff configuration;
- the shared visual with independent alignments;
- tip alignment in all six facings;
- cast point independence from the left hand.

RejectedAttack_ClearsPendingEffect now uses Long Bow as its weapon
without VFX. Document the staff alignment in PlayerCombatArchitecture.md.
```

### 87f67a2ccdeded7e8484377774d270eecc858fa6

[87f67a2ccdeded7e8484377774d270eecc858fa6](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/87f67a2ccdeded7e8484377774d270eecc858fa6)

Date: 2026-09-28T00:47:38-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Abilities, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): migrate Magic Staff to generic directional attack
```

#### Original body

```text
Bake the south-authored MagicStaff_Attack.anim into six one-shot
directional clips (N, NE, NW, S, SE, SW). Add a MagicStaff
DirectionalAttackAnimationSet and move the staff from LegacyRanged to
the generic Attack route (category None).

Being two-handed does not imply that the second hand holds the weapon.
In the staff source the left hand is an independent spell gesture: it
rests on its own side of the body, rotates against the main hand and
never reaches the handle. Long Sword and Zweihander author it turning
rigidly with the main hand on the handle.

Add SecondHandPresentation to WeaponDefinition.Presentation as static
presentation data read only by the generator:
- HoldsSecondaryGrip (default): the existing handle constraint, so
  Long Sword and Zweihander are unchanged.
- FollowsAuthoredMotion: the second hand follows the main hand's rule.
  Its trajectory turns with the facing at its authored key times, and
  its rotation art, depth and timing are kept. It needs no
  SecondaryGripPoint, emits no sorting and leaves the sprite to the
  LeftHand layer.

Validation rejects a second-hand mode on one-handed weapons and only
requires a distinct SecondaryGripPoint for HoldsSecondaryGrip.
LegacyRanged remains for Long Bow and Compound Bow.

Update generator, set, animator and catalog tests, and document the
contract in PlayerCombatArchitecture.md.
```

[ae901da48d3c56eee19a114883a1e84234db5450](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/ae901da48d3c56eee19a114883a1e84234db5450)

Date: 2026-09-28T00:20:33-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Abilities, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(vfx): add Cast Flash attack VFX with Magic Wand alignment
```

#### Original body

```text
Add a third attack VFX archetype for point flashes emitted at the casting
tip, with Magic Wand as its first consumer. The presenter and
AttackVfxDefinition are unchanged: the reach-derived size is now
documented as a length along the pose axis that each archetype
interprets.

- Add CastFlashVfxVisualDefinition: places the art Center on the cast
  point (anchor + axis * size) at native scale, upright and unmirrored.
- Reslice VFX-WandAttack.png into four 96 px cells with centered pivots
  at 16 PPU, like Thrust, and add CastFlashVfx.anim (4 x 50 ms frames).
- Add CastFlashVfxVisual (Center (-0.03125, -0.03125), measured from the
  art) and MagicWandCastFlashAttackVfx: start 0.325s, anchors at the grip
  where the tip stops at 0.35s, grip-to-tip axis as rotation, sorting
  -9 (north) / 21 (south).
- Set Magic Wand BladeTip to (0.03125, 0.46875): the single top pixel of
  the 4x16 px sprite.
- Add CastFlashPresentationTests: clip binding and frame order, shared
  canvas and flash expansion, wand alignment, pose resolution for any
  reach, presenter playback and tip tracking in six facings, and a
  presenter free of archetype and weapon names.
- Move the no-VFX fixture in SwordSlashPresentationTests from Magic Wand
  to Magic Staff.
- Document the Cast Flash archetype and Magic Wand alignment in
  PlayerCombatArchitecture.
```

[22783a6781ab118273172f225f8ae707f24e1a8d](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/22783a6781ab118273172f225f8ae707f24e1a8d)

Date: 2026-09-27T23:52:52-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(vfx): align shared Sword Slash with two-handed Zweihander
```

#### Original body

```text
Add Zweihander as the fourth consumer of SwordSlashVfxVisual through
its own AttackVfxDefinition, reusing the same clip, sprites and visual
definition. No runtime or baker changes.

- Add ZweihanderSlashAttackVfx: start 0.25s, mirrored for the
  counterclockwise strike, sorting -9 (north) / 21 (south).
- Fit the six poses (arc center, rotation, reach offset) to the blade
  tip path of Zweihander's own baked 2H clips, jointly for blade
  reaches 1.0/1.4375/2.2. The same fit reproduces the approved Long
  Sword profile at its 0.08s start.
- Choose the start with the widest worst-frame margin: frame 0
  anticipates the windup apex at 0.3s, frames 1-2 cover the ~190 degree
  strike and frame 3 its end at 0.6s.
- Set Zweihander BladeTip to (0, 1): top pixel row center of the 33 px
  sprite. Size depends only on the grip-to-tip reach.
- Extend SwordSlashPresentationTests: shared visual across four swords,
  Zweihander alignment and 2H contract, rotational sense, blade-tip
  tracing in six facings with geometry variants, independence from
  SecondaryGripPoint, animator phase sampling and alignment isolation.
- Document the Zweihander alignment in PlayerCombatArchitecture.
```


```text
Refactor AttackVfxVisualDefinition into an abstract base class and introduce SlashVfxVisualDefinition and ThrustVfxVisualDefinition to support distinct attack geometry archetypes (arc vs linear).

- Delegate directional pose resolution to AttackVfxVisualDefinition subclasses so each visual archetype controls its own placement and sizing around its anchor.
- Implement SlashVfxVisualDefinition to scale arc-shaped swings by tip radius.
- Implement ThrustVfxVisualDefinition to scale straight-line thrusts along their local +X path (BackX to FrontX) and shift the origin to the stroke anchor.
- Add Thrust VFX art assets (ThrustVfx.anim, VFX-Thrust.png) and configure ThrustVfxVisual and RapierThrustAttackVfx ScriptableObjects.
- Wire RapierWeaponDefinition presentation with RapierThrustAttackVfx, blade tip, and alignment for all 6 directions starting at 0.19s.
- Update SwordSlashPresentationTests and add RapierThrustPresentationTests to cover geometry validation, pose transformations, animator phase sampling, and presenter playback.
- Document polymorphic Attack VFX geometry and Rapier thrust alignment in PlayerCombatArchitecture.
```

### 7e818a685ddf005c4301b92f498d5a0070b78a3c

[7e818a685ddf005c4301b92f498d5a0070b78a3c](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/7e818a685ddf005c4301b92f498d5a0070b78a3c)

Date: 2026-09-27T04:13:12-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Persistence & Backend, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(animation): migrate LongSword to two-handed generic attacks
```

#### Original body

```text
Extend the directional attack baker with a two-handed contract and move
LongSword off the LegacySword fallback onto the generic Attack route.

Two-handed contract:
- DirectionalAnimationGenerator takes the weapon definition; handedness
  comes from it, never from weapon identity. One-handed output is unchanged.
- Two-handed output keeps the authored LeftHandPivot/LeftHand transform
  (rotation art and key times). OffHandGrip stays empty because the weapon
  blocks the Off Hand, and the LeftHand layer keeps owning the hand sprite.
- The second-hand position is derived from the new
  WeaponDefinition.Presentation.SecondaryGripPoint. The baker carries that
  point along the path the presenter uses for the held weapon (MainHandGrip,
  main-hand rotation, facing with its left mirror, angle correction), then
  subtracts the facing's LeftHand idle sprite anchor, so the drawn hand
  lands on the handle.
- The derived position is keyed at the authored key times plus the clip's
  frame grid, so the hand follows the rotating handle within half a pixel.
- The second hand draws over the handle and under the main hand:
  sorting order 25 in front facings, -5 in north facings.
- WeaponDefinition rejects a two-handed generic attack whose secondary grip
  point equals its grip point.

LongSword:
- LongSword_Attack.anim remains the single south source; six one-shot
  clips are generated under Animations/Weapons/Directional/LongSword.
- New LongSword attack animation set; the definition uses category None.
- Main hand grips the handle row under the guard (0, -0.46875) and the
  second hand the last handle row (0, -0.65625).
- Zweihander keeps the LegacySword fallback.

Tests cover the six directions, determinism and GUID-stable rebakes, the
unchanged authored rotation, second-hand placement on the secondary grip,
sorting, the one-handed contract and the new validation rule.
PlayerCombatArchitecture documents the contract.
```


#### Original body

```text
- Se actualizaron los DTOs y `RemoteInventoryService` para incluir `offHand1` y `offHand2`, permitiendo la sincronización del equipamiento de 8 slots con el backend.
- Se modificó `ApplicationStashServiceBootstrapper` para poblar correctamente los slots de Off Hand desde el estado del backend y en los retries de extracción.
- Se corrigió un error que causaba que los cambios de equipamiento en la UI de Inventario (tecla 'I') se perdieran al cerrar sesión:
  - Se agregó un callback `onMutated` en `TownEquipmentMutationEndpoint`.
  - Se implementó `SyncPreparedEquipmentAsync` en `TownInventoryBinder` para enviar los cambios al backend automáticamente con soporte para reconciliación de revisiones.
- Se agregó el alias `heavy_armor_legplate` en el normalizador de identificadores del backend para prevenir errores 422 con personajes heredados.
```

```text
  slash starts at 0.25s and plays unmirrored.
```

```text
with identical content. LegacySword remains for long_sword and zweihander.
```

### bdb0a04f1e4098e593eee2ce8bccb8015bef1745

[bdb0a04f1e4098e593eee2ce8bccb8015bef1745](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/bdb0a04f1e4098e593eee2ce8bccb8015bef1745)

Date: 2026-09-26T00:35:10-03:00 · Classification: Bug Fixes (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, UI, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
fix(vfx): align sword slash with blade trajectory using weapon blade reach
```

#### Original body

```text
The slash used absolute VisualRoot poses (scale 0.65, rotation 0), so its
tip radius (1.05 * 0.65 = 0.68u) sat well inside the measured blade tip arc
(1.0-1.6u around a center ~0.52u ahead of facing) and was not oriented per
facing. Sizes were also tied to Arming Sword proportions.

Make the alignment data-driven and swing-relative:

- WeaponDefinition.Presentation gains BladeTip, in the weapon sprite's local
  units beside GripPoint. BladeReach is their distance.
- AttackVfxDefinition gains TipRadius (radius the blade tip traces through
  the sprite frames). Directional poses now hold the swing arc center,
  rotation, ReachOffset, Mirrored and sorting instead of an absolute scale.
- TryResolvePose derives the uniform scale as
  (ReachOffset + BladeReach) / TipRadius, negated on Y when mirrored.
- PlayerAttackVfxPresenter only applies the resolved pose; it knows no
  weapon or VFX measurements. The effect stays a direct child of VisualRoot,
  so it never inherits the swing twice.
- Weapon validation requires a blade tip distinct from the grip and a
  positive resolved size for every facing.

Arming Sword poses were fitted from its six directional clips (tip-path
circle fit, mean radial residual ~0.055u). The tip arc center stays stable
across blade reaches 0.8-2.0 (drift <= 0.07u), so weapons sharing the swing
animation can share SwordSlashAttackVfx. The rotational-sense fix is kept:
all poses remain mirrored.

Tests:
- AttackVfx_TracesBladeTipForSwordAndVariantGeometries samples the real
  blade tip with production grip/facing mator
  <= 0.1u) and per-frame angular coverage in all six facings, for Arming
  Sword and short/long geometry variants sharing the same Attack VFX.
- SharedAttackVfx_ResizesFromBladeReachWith
  WeaponWithAttackVfx_RequiresBladeTipDistinctFromGrip cover resolution                                                 and validation.
- Existing pose and configuration tests updated to the new contract.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md describes the new Attack VFX contract.
```

### afb66ca73d775cde0c2b147161e688efee125746

[afb66ca73d775cde0c2b147161e688efee125746](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/afb66ca73d775cde0c2b147161e688efee125746)

Date: 2026-09-25T22:52:42-03:00 · Classification: Bug Fixes (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Build & Tooling, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
fix(vfx): match sword slash sweep direction to swing in south facings
```

#### Original body

```text
The canonical VFX-Slash sequence sweeps clockwise around its pivot, while
every ArmingSword directional attack clip rotates the hand counter-clockwise
(shared RightHand z curve: 0 -> -49.2 -> 57.5 -> 69.0; the generator only
rotates hand position per direction). North poses were already mirrored, so
N/NE/NW played in the swing's direction, but S/SE/SW were unmirrored and
played reversed.

- Mirror the S/SE/SW poses in SwordSlashAttackVfx (scale.y 0.65 -> -0.65).
  Position, rotation, sorting and SwordSlashVfx.anim are unchanged.
- Replace the front/back pose-group assertions with a data-driven contract:
  AttackVfx_SweepsInSameRotationalSenseAsWeaponSwing applies each configured
  DirectionalPose through the presenter and compares the signed angular
  sweep of the VFX frame centroids with the main-hand grip sweep during the
  VFX window, both in Animator root space. It covers every catalog weapon
  with an Attack VFX and does not assume a mirror axis or weapon.
- ConfirmedSwordAttack_CapturesConfiguredDirectionalPose now asserts the
  presenter applies the configured pose for each direction.
- Keep a separate configuration test pinning the serialized pose values.

Spatial alignment of the slash with the blade is out of scope and left for
a follow-up.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Fix: Corregir fallos de validación del Codec en Extracciones y Reclamo de Misiones
```

#### Original body

```text
Fix: Corregir fallos de validación del Codec en Extracciones y Reclamo de Misiones

- En `HydrateSnapshot` se vacía `AppliedExtractionReceipts` antes de agregar el recibo del backend para evitar su acumulación en sesiones consecutivas, previniendo errores "Applied extraction receipts contain invalid or duplicate data".
- En `LocalProfileStore.TryClaimMission` se genera y encadena un `ProgressionReceipt` tras la recompensa de experiencia para mantener la coherencia del historial de progresión y superar el Codec V5.
- Removido log obsoleto en `LocalProfileSaveCodec`.
- Agregados EditMode Tests para ambas correcciones.
```

```text
feat(missions): Implementar UI del Tablón de Misiones en Town (TASK-167 / Etapa 7)
```

#### Original body

```text
feat(missions): Implementar UI del Tablón de Misiones en Town (TASK-167 / Etapa 7)

- Añadidos controladores de interfaz para el tablón de contratos:
  - MissionBoardUI: Administra la visualización de contratos disponibles, selección, lectura del catálogo de misiones desde LocalProfileStore y acción de aceptar.
  - MissionBoardEntryUI: Maneja cada tarjeta/fila de misión en la lista con estados visuales (disponible, activa, completada).
  - MissionObjectiveEntryUI: Renderiza cada objetivo por fases con estado de progreso y toggle visual.
  - MissionRewardEntryUI: Presenta las recompensas asociadas al contrato (oro, exp, items).
  - MissionBoardHotkeyToggle: Atajo de teclado (tecla M) para pruebas rápidas de apertura/cierre en Town.
- Creados los prefabs modulares de UI para el tablón y sus elementos en Assets/Prefabs/UI/Missions/.
- Expuesta la propiedad pública MissionCatalog en LocalProfileStore para consumo directo de la vista.
- Integrado el panel en la escena Lobby-Town.
```

### b1da6f2ff47b123362260be2d71b3f1ee78f4461

[b1da6f2ff47b123362260be2d71b3f1ee78f4461](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/b1da6f2ff47b123362260be2d71b3f1ee78f4461)

Date: 2026-09-17T23:27:54-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Persistence & Backend, Build & Tooling, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat: implement universal inventory drag and drop system
```

#### Original body

```text
- Introduced semantic struct-based payload definitions for drag-and-drop actions across inventory, stash, equipment, and container panels.

- Wired UGUI pointer events to the existing MVP architecture via RaidLootPanelView and RaidInventorySlotView.

- Refactored LobbyStashPresenter and RaidInventoryPresenter to natively translate DropReceived events into remote/local mutations (equip, unequip, move to stash).

- Fixed item duplication exploits during local Stash-to-Equipment assignments by ensuring TryTransferToLoadout resolves correctly before equipping.

- Aligned DragPreviewView to render perfectly under the cursor independent of Canvas root configurations using local position translation.
```

### 866499c670a28ccd7073dac63a073e181221ed79

[866499c670a28ccd7073dac63a073e181221ed79](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/866499c670a28ccd7073dac63a073e181221ed79)

Date: 2026-09-15T16:27:47-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Extraction, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, Persistence & Backend, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(backend, unity): implement host-signed authoritative extraction results
```

#### Original body

```text
Este commit cierra el ciclo del issue #361 al convertir al Host de
Photon Fusion en un productor validado criptográficamente (MVP) de
AuthoritativeExtractionResult, desbloqueando el flujo de extracción en
producción sin servidores dedicados.
Backend:
- Agregado webhookSecret a variables de entorno.
- Nuevo endpoint POST /character/raid/extraction-result.
- Validación HMAC-SHA256 en RaidResultService.
Unity:
- Agregado WebhookSecret a BackendConfiguration.
- Lógica de firmado HMAC-SHA256 en RemoteInventoryService.
- PlayerExtractionLootSaver ahora publica el resultado antes del commit si es Host.
```

### 930162c9e5407e022d70de75be114d8d605f374b

[930162c9e5407e022d70de75be114d8d605f374b](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/930162c9e5407e022d70de75be114d8d605f374b)

Date: 2026-09-14T02:20:54-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Networking & Sessions, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add raid duo teammate HUD projection
```

#### Original body

```text
This change adds frozen duo teammate resolution from the launch roster and projects the teammate's health into the local HUD. It introduces `RaidInitialAffiliationSnapshot.TryGetTeammateProfileId`, binds a new `RaidTeammateHudPresenter`/`RaidTeammateHudView`, and wires it into `LocalPlayerHudBinder`.

The presenter resolves the matching `NetworkRaidParticipant` by stable `ProfileId`, reads live avatar health, falls back to extracted-health cache or defeat state, and keeps a placeholder while the teammate is unavailable. It includes edit-mode and play-mode coverage plus architecture notes documenting the duo teammate projection lifecycle.
```

### 0d7f3e66dd3092b435adb65d7e624c05cb4f551e

[0d7f3e66dd3092b435adb65d7e624c05cb4f551e](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/0d7f3e66dd3092b435adb65d7e624c05cb4f551e)

Date: 2026-09-14T01:19:55-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Split player spawns into team-based areas
```

#### Original body

```text
Refactors scene spawn configuration to move players out of generic SpawnGroupDefinition into dedicated PlayerSpawnAreaDefinition collections, and marks SpawnGroupType.Players as unsupported in initial world-group dispatch. NetworkSpawnManager now tracks player areas separately, validates them against scene ownership, uses fresh-session-only preflight checks, and resolves player spawn transforms via team/participant assignment rules. RaidParticipantSpawnRules was expanded to validate full fresh launch context, enforce unique transform/position usage, and deterministically map participants to area/point pairs by team appearance and intra-team order. Updated gameplay scene data, architecture docs, and edit-mode tests to cover the new model and reject legacy generic player groups.
```

### 3a091ee723c23e5cf96bfa2ee5507b85d37f5dc8

[3a091ee723c23e5cf96bfa2ee5507b85d37f5dc8](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/3a091ee723c23e5cf96bfa2ee5507b85d37f5dc8)

Date: 2026-09-14T00:42:16-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Networking & Sessions, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add duo party continuation restoration
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduce `TownPartyContinuationContext` and an authority-side `TownPartyContinuationClaimRegistry` to preserve and restore solo/duo Town parties after runner replacement. The session coordinator now keeps a pending continuation claim, validates restoration against the recreated Town roster, and supports explicit abandonment.

`TownRaidPreparationDirectory` now coordinates claim/ack/invalidations via RPCs, rebuild-triggered claim epochs, and authority-side restoration spawning when all required members claim. While continuation is pending, ordinary create/join/ready/start requests are blocked, and the presenter/view show a pending-party state with an abandon action.

Town preparation capacity is now explicitly capped at 2 (`TownRaidPreparationRules.MaxMembers`) while keeping raid session max participants unchanged. Related networking/controller logic, tests, and architecture docs were updated to reflect duo-only preparation and continuation claim behavior.
```

### 727e8bc7168294d008e392838a521328ed0748a7

[727e8bc7168294d008e392838a521328ed0748a7](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/727e8bc7168294d008e392838a521328ed0748a7)

Date: 2026-09-13T23:48:44-03:00 · Classification: Bug Fixes (explicit) · Systems: Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, Persistence & Backend

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
fix: persist prepared equipment changes to backend on equip/unequip
```

#### Original body

```text
El equipamiento (prepared equipment) se mutaba solo en el estado local
al equipar/desequipar desde el stash, a diferencia de las transferencias
stash<->loadout que sí sincronizan con el backend. Como resultado, el
equipo sobrevivía dentro de una misma sesión de juego pero se perdía
tras logout/login, porque nunca llegaba a persistirse vía
PUT /character/me/inventory/prepared-equipment.

OnPreparedEquipmentAssignmentRequested y OnPreparedEquipmentClearRequested
ahora, tras la mutación local exitosa, sincronizan el estado resultante
al backend a través de RemoteInventoryService.UpdatePreparedEquipmentAsync
(endpoint ya existente pero nunca invocado).

Archivo modificado:
- Assets/Scripts/Stash/LobbyStashPresenter.cs
```

#### Changed paths

```text
Project Grimhold/Assets/Scripts/Stash/LobbyStashPresenter.cs
```

### 8e499c1576bbeb5b6fef8222f47f83cedb3e260c

[8e499c1576bbeb5b6fef8222f47f83cedb3e260c](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/8e499c1576bbeb5b6fef8222f47f83cedb3e260c)

Date: 2026-09-11T01:18:19-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, UI, Persistence & Backend, Input, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(combat): add sustained off-hand shield defense
```

#### Original body

```text
Add validated shield loot definitions, Off Hand equipment compatibility, persistence support, and atomic interaction with existing two-handed weapon rules.

Replicate authoritative defense from secondary input, prioritize defense over attacks, and reduce frontal physical and magical damage by 50 percent inside an inclusive 120-degree cone after armor mitigation. True damage remains unaffected.

Register the Training Shield in Raid catalogs and container drops, wire the Fusion controller into NetworkPlayer, expand deterministic/configuration tests, and document the combat architecture.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Add equipment-derived runtime stats and mitigation
```

#### Original body

```text
This change adds pure calculators for armor mitigation, equipment modifier aggregation, and weapon scaling resolution, then combines them into PlayerRuntimeStatistics used by player health, stamina, and damage mitigation. It also updates progression defaults/configuration to include maximum Mana and equipment-derived modifiers, refreshes the architecture docs, and adds edit/play mode coverage for the new equipment and combat behavior.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Add armor loot and weapon scaling data
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduces `ArmorDefinition`, maximum resource modifiers, and canonical weapon instance scaling slots with grade-based coefficients. Updates loot validation and weapon definitions to enforce matching natural scaling, adds armor references to armor loot assets, and expands edit-mode tests and combat architecture docs.
```

```text
- Updated Presenters to query audio configurations safely using string keys (e.g. "Swing", "TakeDamage").

- Created WeaponAudioPresenter observing ICombatController.AttackPerformed.
- Created EnemyAudioPresenter observing CharacterBase.Health and IsAlive.
- Integrated both presenters with the global AudioManager API.
```

### ac134e3e671f6577d2cbb1b3510e86d3dc122cd0

[ac134e3e671f6577d2cbb1b3510e86d3dc122cd0](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/ac134e3e671f6577d2cbb1b3510e86d3dc122cd0)

Date: 2026-09-09T16:26:29-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add runtime attribute override flow for raids
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduces a development-only runtime attribute override system that composes session offsets over persistent raid attributes without touching profile persistence. Adds `RuntimeAttributeOverrideState/Session`, a replicated `RuntimeAttributeOverrideNetworkController`, and a local developer IMGUI panel in Town/Raid prefabs.

`NetworkRaidParticipant` now exposes effective attributes (plus persistent read and revision), and consumers were updated to react to override revisions: weapon equipment revalidates requirements/scaling, player max health caches by revision, and health is clamped after max-health decreases. Includes prefab wiring, edit/play mode coverage for override behavior, and architecture docs updates to reflect the effective-attribute model.
```

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Refactor equipment to weapon sets with off-hands
```

#### Original body

```text
Reworked player equipment from 6 slots to 8 slots by replacing legacy weapon slots with Set A/Set B main-hand + off-hand, introducing `WeaponSetSlot` and weapon handedness (`OneHanded`/`TwoHanded`). Updated equip/mutation rules, input actions, active-weapon selection, raid admission payloads (codec v9), and local profile persistence (schema v4) to carry the new model and validate two-handed/off-hand constraints. UI/prefabs, stash/town flows, tests, and architecture docs were aligned to explicit slot targeting and blocked off-hand behavior.
```

```text
Update architecture documentation and focused EditMode/PlayMode coverage for composition, persistence, ownership integrity, lifecycle, and context positioning.
```

### 33f7c5b915dcd94768fad4e8f14b12d7ca905050

[33f7c5b915dcd94768fad4e8f14b12d7ca905050](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/33f7c5b915dcd94768fad4e8f14b12d7ca905050)

Date: 2026-09-03T21:35:21-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Combat, Extraction, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Defer loot generation and apply raid luck bonus
```

#### Original body

```text
Reworks spawned loot containers and breakables to replicate a pending generation descriptor (seed + additional loot chance) and resolve it exactly once at first valid interaction or fatal breakable damage, with terminal Resolved/Failed states to prevent rerolls. Adds raid-wide effective luck calculation (average derived basis points from the admitted cohort), extends the roller with deterministic optional bonus-stack logic and headroom validation, raises the initial max luck bonus cap to 30%, and updates prefab wiring, tests, and architecture docs to match the new flow.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Refine raid lifecycle and persistence docs
```

#### Original body

```text
Reworked several architecture documents to align on the current Vertical Slice model: durable backend-owned character persistence, stable remote CharacterId/ProfileId identity, and clearer separation between temporary Raid simulation and metagame state. The raid/session docs now define the participant-vs-avatar ownership model, frozen admission flow, fail-closed spawning, phase transitions (including Closing), and Host Migration restore/rebind boundaries. Combat and HUD docs were updated to match these decisions, including defeated-avatar behavior and attribute-derived effective max health.
```

### 4bb460b5ad718cebe57818429b1d217c644a0fd9

[4bb460b5ad718cebe57818429b1d217c644a0fd9](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/4bb460b5ad718cebe57818429b1d217c644a0fd9)

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add networked stamina and sprint support
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduces `PlayerStaminaNetworkController` and `StaminaResourceRules` to own replicated stamina state, regeneration delay, exhaustion behavior, and max stamina derivation from admitted attributes. Movement now reads a new Sprint input action/button and applies a sprint speed multiplier only when continuous stamina spend succeeds. The raid HUD and local binder were extended to present stamina value/fill and exhaustion state, and player prefabs were wired with the new stamina component and references. Adds edit/play mode coverage for stamina rules, sprint input transport, execution order, HUD stamina rendering, and migration-related stamina restoration behavior, plus architecture docs updates.
```

[812fec4ea52aef73af94e2c30e7d1fc39d59fc15](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/812fec4ea52aef73af94e2c30e7d1fc39d59fc15)

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Refactor: Decouple PreparedEquipment from Loadout to fix persistence and visual duplication
```

#### Original body

```text
- Changed backend `InventoryService.updatePreparedEquipment` to compute equipment diffs, deducting from Loadout/Stash on equip and refunding on unequip.
- Refactored `LocalProfileStore` in Unity to explicitly remove items from Loadout/Stash when equipping, instead of keeping them as references.
- Updated `PreparedEquipmentLoadout.TryValidate` and `LocalProfileSaveCodec` to stop checking equipment ownership against the Loadout, as equipment slots are now the exclusive owners of their items.
- Improved QoL for "Leave All": unequipping items is no longer forced when transferring the backpack to the Stash.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Refactor attack stats into runtime parameters
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduces `AttackExecutionParameters` and moves damage, cooldown, range, damage type, and knockback out of shared `AttackConfig` assets into runtime/executor-owned data. `WeaponDefinition` now owns player weapon combat stats, while melee/ranged configs keep only reusable behavior settings. Updated player equipment wiring, trap behavior ownership, prefab/scriptable data, gizmo range math, and added coverage to preserve legacy combat behavior and cooldown continuity.
```

```text
Enforce weapon attribute requirements
```

#### Original body

```text
Adds `WeaponAttributeRequirements` to weapon definitions and enforces them end-to-end across equip requests, prepared loadouts, reservation creation/reuse, and rollback paths. Equipment/stash/preparation result enums and UI messages now surface `AttributeRequirementsNotMet`, and network weapon activation now depends on admitted participant attributes via `RaidAvatarParticipantLink`.

Also updates weapon and loot assets for MVP balancing (weapon requirements, extraction values, loot table weights, raid loot value entries), wires the player prefab dependency, and expands edit/play mode tests plus architecture docs to cover the new eligibility behavior.
```

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Derive player max health from participant stats
```

#### Original body

```text
Character max health is now resolved through a virtual path: `CharacterBase` uses an effective max for spawn initialization, max-health exposure, and healing caps, while `PlayerCharacter` derives and caches that value from the linked participant’s frozen attributes (with prefab fallback when unresolved/invalid). PlayMode coverage was expanded to verify NPC prefab max health remains unchanged, player vitality drives fresh health/healing/HUD limits, and initial HUD expectations are explicit. Architecture docs were updated to capture the local max-health projection behavior and host-migration restoration semantics.
```

```text
- New UI component LogoutButtonPresenter to trigger logout from Town, added to prefabs/scenes.
- LoginFlowController.ExecuteLogoutAsync to call backend logout, reset stash and clear auth state.
- AuthenticationClient.PostLogoutAsync to POST /auth/logout.
- ApplicationStashServiceBootstrapper.ResetForLogout to teardown in-memory services.
- SessionConnectionCoordinator.ReturnToMainMenuAsync and state machine updates to allow MainMenu transitions.
- LoginPanelView.ClearFields and MainMenuController fixes for coordinator lookup.
- Backend: POST /auth/logout route + AuthService.logout no-op (placeholder for token revocation).
- Docs updated describing logout lifecycle.
```

### 2df36961e74afa1489c93f757699620d23e005b5

[2df36961e74afa1489c93f757699620d23e005b5](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/2df36961e74afa1489c93f757699620d23e005b5)

Date: 2026-09-01T16:56:38-03:00 · Classification: Features (explicit) · Systems: Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
feat(equipment): integrate LightArmor, ForestRanger and FireMage sets
```

#### Original body

```text
Replicate the validated HeavyArmor/ArmyRanger/ArcaneMage pipeline for
three new modular armor sets. Each set maps its pieces onto the four
existing slots (Helmet/Armor/Gloves/Boots) and stays freely combinable;
no new slot and no per-set skin.

Art: import and re-slice 180 sprite sheets (60 per set) to Grid By Cell
Size 96x96 with the reference import settings (PPU 16, Point filter, no
compression, Clamp, alpha transparency, center pivot). The sheets had
been auto-imported trimmed at PPU 100; re-gridded while preserving the
existing sprite ids so references stay stable.

Definitions: add 12 LootDefinition assets (4 per set) with stable new
ids, each embedding an EquipmentVisualDefinition of base->equipped
sprite mappings — 84 per single-part slot, 168 for gloves (left+right),
420 per set, 1260 new mappings total. Icon/world sprite = Idle-S frame 0
(right glove for the Gloves slot). Appended to LootDefinitionCatalog
(22 -> 34) without reordering existing entries, and to the productive
loot table with the same weight (6) as the MVP pieces (21 -> 33).

Tests: extend ArmorSetCatalogTests to cover the six sets — validity,
categories, unique ids, deterministic catalog resolution, full
Idle/Walk x 6 directions coverage, left/right hand completeness, no
duplicate/null/cross-part mappings, 420 per set, and loot-table
membership.
```

### 0340b23ca8491a7e3550e87886c78f8f4f79734c

[0340b23ca8491a7e3550e87886c78f8f4f79734c](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/0340b23ca8491a7e3550e87886c78f8f4f79734c)

Date: 2026-09-01T16:53:21-03:00 · Classification: Bug Fixes (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Build & Tooling, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
fix(presentation): reserve sorting slots for equipment layers
```

#### Original body

```text
The modular character rendered each equipment layer at base+1, but the
base body parts used consecutive sorting orders (Legs=1, Body=2,
LeftHand=3, Head=4), leaving no gap. Every equipment layer therefore
landed on the next base part: Boots tied Body, Armor tied LeftHand and
LeftGlove tied Head. Equal sortingOrder makes the draw order
non-deterministic, most visibly the Boots (leg armor) clipping against
the Body.

Re-space the base parts so each reserves a free slot above it while
keeping their relative order identical (Legs=0, Body=2, LeftHand=4,
Head=6; Body and RightHand=30 left untouched to preserve the weapon
relationship). Equipment now lands in the gaps with no ties:
Legs<Boots<Body<Armor<LeftHand<LeftGlove<Head<Helmet.

Extract the base+offset into EquipmentLayerSortingRule so the layer
tracking stays dynamic and per-slot (no per-set hardcoding), and add
EditMode tests: offset preserved as base order changes, base parts have
distinct orders, no equipment layer collides with a foreign base part,
and the intended back-to-front stack is preserved.
```

#### Changed paths

```text
Project Grimhold/Assets/Prefabs/NetworkPlayer.prefab
Project Grimhold/Assets/Scripts/Player/Presentation/EquipmentLayerSortingRule.cs
Project Grimhold/Assets/Scripts/Player/Presentation/EquipmentLayerSortingRule.cs.meta
```
